content.title: Too Hot for Dignity
content.narrative:
YY stepped onto the sunny bark shelf and stepped right back off.

"Absolutely not," he said.

The bark had turned hot by midmorning, the kind of hot that came up through the paws and made a squirrel reconsider every heroic plan he had invented while still in shade.

The fern line smelled cooler. Damp. Less glorious. More alive.

YY looked at the shelf. The shelf had the best view and probably no food. The fern line had shadows and probably seeds. This was not a hard decision, but YY gave it a serious face anyway.

He retreated with what he chose to call strategic elegance. Halfway down the shaded root, he found fern seeds caught where the soil dipped. Not many. Enough.

The hot shelf stayed up there being bright and useless. YY stayed below, eating in the shade with his tail over his paws.

Dignity, he decided, was better when it came with breakfast.
content.state_note: YY avoided the overheated shelf, lost a little health to the heat, and found a cooler food line under the ferns.
content.summary: YY abandoned the hot bark shelf and found fern-line seeds in the shade.
content.world_anchor: On 2026-05-18, WTAP forecast low-90s heat building across the Mid-Ohio Valley before midweek storms cooled the region down.
